text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz said he recognised the importance of religious education but would not allow the country to become another Iran.
- Yilmaz is expected to set 1997 hazlenut price as $2 a kg.
- Navy chief, Admiral Guven Erkaya said the military was not planning a coup against the former Islamist government.
- Coalition junior party leader Husamettin Cindoruk complained that coalition leaders in the Motherland Party did not consult him on government appointments.
- Foreign investors are optimistic about Turkey's future economic performance.
- Many non-governmental organisations are contributing money to help the government's eight-year education plans.
- A Turkish state security court began investigations into the National Youth Foundation known as the youth wing of the Islam-based Welfare Party.
- The Treasury will announce its new borrowing plans in September.
- The finance minister says a secularist education plan will cost $6 billion in the first three years.
